events.title: USA PATRIOT Act signed into law
events.summary: President Bush signed the USA PATRIOT Act on October 26, 2001 — expanding government surveillance powers including wiretap, business-record, and pen-register authorities in the wake of the September 11 attacks.
events.about: The PATRIOT Act reshaped how telecoms and internet companies handled law-enforcement requests — and later fueled debates over bulk [metadata] collection revealed by Edward Snowden. Section 215 business records and national security letters became routine compliance workflows for cloud providers storing user data.

narrative.whyChosen: The PATRIOT Act set the legal framework for post-9/11 digital surveillance that Snowden later exposed.
narrative.whyImportant: It forced tech companies to build legal-compliance teams for government data requests at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Law enforcement argued pre-9/11 tools were too slow for tracking terrorists across phones and the internet.
